unresolved.evidence: Static suite arithmetic is correct: both gate judges are 600s (judge.toml:4), so sequential 600+600=1200<1500; scored judges are 9000+900+900=10800<11100; 1500+11100=12600<13200, leaving 600s outside suites. test.sh:207 explicitly uses --max-concurrent-agent 1. Agent/build budgets are canonical 7200/600s (task.toml:18,21); no measured cold-build or builder completion establishes sufficiency. However liveness does not have a nested wall-clock bound: test.sh:50 and :138 call urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=2).read(), and :116-122 / :171-177 perform 120 iterations with 0.25s sleep. Two full socket timeouts per iteration take approximately 120*(2+2+0.25)=510s, excluding process overhead; the restart wrapper instead kills its helper after 55s (restart_mcp.py:11,39), so that inner wait does not fit its outer budget. A response that continuously delivers body bytes need not finish .read() at all; the initial readiness call has no surrounding wall-clock timeout. Cleanup also has an unbounded wait after SIGTERM (test.sh:33-38), so the 600s apparent verifier margin is not a guaranteed total bound. These bytes are unchanged shared-template code: current and frozen-template test.sh both hash bd68259276ca4b034654efc8a1723a4e702ed62dbe590af6201565f43eabe5aa; restart_mcp.py both hash 03c1426f00e451f4d86b7547761715328c63cdf299f5f812f46c9fa3b44979b5. Offline Python 3.12 socket reproduction used a localhost server returning seven bytes at 0.5s intervals, then the exact urlopen(...,timeout=2).read() expression: it completed in 3.000s, proving 2s is not a total-request bound. The first local attempt hit the host proxy (HTTP 400); the corrected run explicitly disabled proxies for this local fixture and succeeded. This is a library-semantics reproduction, not an execution of the frozen verifier container. Positive current golden evidence: actual-restart.json reports one successful canonical MCP call in 5.599140s (SHA256 8ad9a4a2e7aada61c4f4a45a07574b540de4e9c0fb7f9ff9f2c8556bc5080ada), which does not exercise the slow/unending response case. Independently, required full configured workload remains unmeasured: raw-evidence-index.json explicitly lists Full configured judge completion/workload as not_measured and runtime-evidence.json is absent. The current golden RESULTS.json says browser_driver=direct pinned Playwright, paid_provider=false and wall_seconds=116.595608784; host RESULT.json says provider_or_platform=false and wall_seconds=119.594. Their verified hashes are c7e553fb3c51a25f29e60ef1d417f3471547c0b37e4b1887d4c2f8eeee97050d and b119ada03db5a35e8c41de84cb7695f286726a11e46dd44c54aefdbd2a47b8e7. A nonanswering listener also makes the restart readiness loop capable of roughly 510s while its MCP parent aborts at 55s. A SIGTERM-ignoring app can leave final cleanup waiting indefinitely. These do not pass the row merely because suite constants add up. Conforming-alternative workload risk (not an observed failure): a complete app with legitimate app-specific dialogs and different controls can require additional browser discovery and permitted retries across the 23 protocols; source action estimates and the 116.6s scripted golden cannot rule out the configured LLM judge exceeding 9000s and losing grading evidence.
